title: Audio and music basics: waveforms to spectrograms

questions.q: A pure 8000 Hz tone is sampled at 10000 Hz. At what frequency does a spectrum show it?
options: 8000 Hz, sampling does not change frequency
2000 Hz, because it folds back as |f − sr · round(f / sr)|
5000 Hz, the Nyquist frequency
It disappears, because it is above Nyquist
questions.answer: 2000 Hz, because it folds back as |f − sr · round(f / sr)|
questions.why: Shannon's sampling theorem holds only for frequencies below sr / 2 = 5000 Hz. Above that a tone aliases. The lab finds the peak at 2000 Hz for 8000 Hz, exactly as the formula predicts for all six tones.

questions.q: What does the Hann window buy over a rectangular window in the lab's 440 Hz test?
options: Narrower bins
A higher peak
Far less leakage away from the peak, -91.2 dB against -37.4 dB at 20 bins, and a refined estimate within 1 Hz
A longer frame
questions.answer: Far less leakage away from the peak, -91.2 dB against -37.4 dB at 20 bins, and a refined estimate within 1 Hz
questions.why: Both windows put the peak in bin 10, 430.66 Hz. The bin width is the same, 43.07 Hz. With the Hann window the parabola through the three bins gives 440.63 Hz, and with the rectangular one 434.00 Hz.

questions.q: Two equal tones at 440 and 460 Hz are analysed with different frame lengths. What does the lab show?
options: Longer frames always give a worse picture
Frame length does not matter, only the sample rate does
A 1024-sample frame (23 ms) shows one hump with a -0.9 dB dip, and an 8192-sample frame (186 ms) separates them with a -28.1 dB dip, at the cost of time detail
Both tones are found at every frame length
questions.answer: A 1024-sample frame (23 ms) shows one hump with a -0.9 dB dip, and an 8192-sample frame (186 ms) separates them with a -28.1 dB dip, at the cost of time detail
questions.why: Bin width is sr / n_fft, so a longer frame resolves closer tones, but it spans more time, so events inside it cannot be placed as precisely.

questions.q: EmptyLatentAudio is asked for 47.6 seconds. How long is the latent, and why can the duration not be exact?
options: 1024 frames, because the length is round((seconds · 44100 / 2048) / 2) · 2, an even number, so it covers 47.554 s
47600 frames, one per millisecond
2048 frames, one per stride
44100 frames, one per sample
questions.answer: 1024 frames, because the length is round((seconds · 44100 / 2048) / 2) · 2, an even number, so it covers 47.554 s
questions.why: Each latent frame stands for 2048 samples at 44100 Hz, about 46.4 ms. Rounding to an even count gives 1024 frames, which covers 47.554 s. At 10 s the same rule gives 216 frames, 10.031 s.

questions.q: What does VAEDecodeAudio do to the level of the decoded audio?
options: It leaves it untouched
It divides it by max(1, 5 × its standard deviation), so anything with a standard deviation above 0.2 comes out at 0.2
It raises quiet audio to a fixed peak
It clips it at ±1
questions.answer: It divides it by max(1, 5 × its standard deviation), so anything with a standard deviation above 0.2 comes out at 0.2
questions.why: The lab's sines with amplitudes 0.05 and 0.2 are unchanged. Amplitudes 0.3 and 0.9 both end at standard deviation 0.2000.

questions.q: Why must audio be low-pass filtered before dropping every second sample when halving the sample rate?
options: To make the file smaller
Because the tones above the new Nyquist frequency would otherwise fold back, a 6 kHz tone coming out at 2 kHz with amplitude 1.0000
Because the Hann window needs it
Because the mel scale requires it
questions.answer: Because the tones above the new Nyquist frequency would otherwise fold back, a 6 kHz tone coming out at 2 kHz with amplitude 1.0000
questions.why: At 8 kHz the Nyquist frequency is 4 kHz. With the filter first, the lab's remaining amplitude is 0.0000. ComfyUI's resample in comfy/audio.py is a bandlimited sinc resampler for this reason.
